subject: general
question: Which newspaper did Mahatma Gandhi start in South Africa?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Opinion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The newspaper Indian Opinion,** founded by **Mahatma Gandhi** and published in **Durban, South Africa**, was representative of a created imagined nationality.
 
• The newspaper, which is experimental in the true sense, is frequently described as anti-commodity, copyright-free, and slow-moving.
 
• It contradicted popular perceptions of what constitutes a "newspaper," which generally comprises news pieces, editorials, reports from outstation reporters, and analyses, among other things.
 
• Once a week, Indian Opinion was printed in four languages: **English, Gujarati, Tamil, **and **Hindi.**
 
• The current study examines Gandhi's publications in the Indian Opinion from June to December 1903, tracing his concept of an Indian identity that transcends linguistic and religious differences.
 
• These essays reveal a great deal about his conception of Indianness, both civilizational and geographical.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Indian Sociologist** was an early twentieth-century Indian nationalist publication. An Organ of Freedom and Political, Social, and Religious Reform was its subtitle.
 
• **Commonweal** was a socialist journal published in the United Kingdom that was launched in 1885 by the newly formed Socialist League.
 
• **The National Herald** is an Indian daily produced by The Associated Journals Ltd and controlled by the Indian National Congress's Young India Limited.
